content.value_statement: Real-time shader work often fails from missing math details or WebGL2 differences. This skill gives structured GLSL techniques, adaptation rules, and debugging guidance.
actual_capabilities: Routes shader requests to focused technique guides for 36 graphics topics.
Generates ShaderToy-style GLSL concepts with WebGL2 adaptation guidance.
Covers ray marching, SDF modeling, lighting, particles, fluids, terrain, water, and post-processing.
Explains common WebGL2 pitfalls including fragment coordinates, main wrappers, uniforms, and function order.
Provides performance budgets for ray steps, volume samples, FBM layers, and nested loops.
limitations: It does not execute, profile, or visually validate generated shaders.
It is not a complete WebGL engine, asset pipeline, or scene editor.
Complex simulations still need tuning for each browser, GPU, and canvas size.
Non-WebGL targets may require manual syntax and API adaptation.

use_cases.title: Prototype Procedural Scenes
use_cases.description: Create raymarched SDF scenes, fractals, procedural patterns, and stylized visual effects from text requirements.

use_cases.title: Build Game Visual Effects
use_cases.description: Draft WebGL2 water, terrain, particles, lighting, shadows, bloom, and camera effects for interactive projects.

use_cases.title: Debug Shader Porting Issues
use_cases.description: Adapt ShaderToy conventions to standalone WebGL2 pages and avoid common compile and runtime failures.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Shader
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small visual effect.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple WebGL2 fragment shader concept for a procedural animated background. Use one primary technique and include setup notes.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a ShaderToy Idea
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt a ShaderToy-style effect to standalone WebGL2. Include the required uniform mapping, main wrapper, and likely compile pitfalls.

prompt_templates.title: Combine Multiple Techniques
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a real-time scene that combines SDF geometry, soft shadows, ambient occlusion, atmospheric fog, and tone mapping. Keep performance practical.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize and Diagnose
prompt_templates.prompt: Review a slow or blank WebGL2 shader workflow. Identify likely causes, performance risks, and visual debugging outputs to isolate the problem.

output_examples.input: Create a raymarched glass orb scene with soft shadows and bloom.
output: A technique plan using SDF geometry, ray marching, normal estimation, lighting, shadows, and post-processing.
WebGL2 adaptation notes for uniforms, fragment coordinates, and shader entry points.
Performance limits for marching steps, shadow samples, and bloom passes.

output_examples.input: Port a ShaderToy fluid effect into a standalone browser page.
output: A multipass buffer plan with ping-pong state, mouse input handling, and frame timing.
Browser setup guidance for WebGL2, framebuffer formats, resize handling, and fallback messaging.
Debug checks for NaN velocity, unsupported extensions, and excessive sampling.

output_examples.input: Improve a procedural terrain shader that looks repetitive.
output: Suggestions for FBM variation, domain warping, texture repetition avoidance, and atmospheric depth cues.
A checklist for balancing quality against ray steps, noise octaves, and normal estimation cost.

best_practices: Name the target platform, browser context, resolution, and performance budget before requesting a shader.
Ask for one primary technique plus a few supporting techniques instead of combining every effect.
Request WebGL2 adaptation and debugging notes when the output must run outside ShaderToy.
anti_patterns: Requesting all techniques in one shader without a visual priority or performance target.
Mixing ShaderToy and WebGL2 conventions without asking for explicit adaptation rules.
Ignoring loop limits, ray step counts, and sampling budgets for browser-based rendering.

faq.question: Does this skill run or preview shaders?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and shader development patterns, but it does not execute or visually test the result.

faq.question: Can it create standalone WebGL2 pages?
faq.answer: It includes adaptation rules for standalone WebGL2 pages, including uniforms, canvas setup, and common compile issues.

faq.question: Is it only for ShaderToy?
faq.answer: No. The references use ShaderToy-style concepts, but the skill explains how to adapt them to WebGL2.

faq.question: Which shader topics are covered?
faq.answer: It covers SDFs, ray marching, lighting, shadows, particles, fluids, terrain, water, noise, post-processing, and more.

faq.question: Can it help with performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides practical budgets for ray steps, sampling loops, FBM octaves, and browser rendering limits.

faq.question: Does it replace graphics engineering review?
faq.answer: No. Complex effects still need browser testing, profiling, visual review, and device-specific tuning.
